source: SPEED design-review prototype starter library v0.1 (unreviewed; BRD 16.2, FR-HAZ-05)

materials.name: 4-Fluorobenzaldehyde
materials.note: Combustible liquid. Oxidises slowly in air on storage.

materials.name: Piperidine
materials.note: Flammable, toxic base. Controlled precursor in some jurisdictions (check locally).

materials.name: Isopropanol
materials.note: Listed as a peroxide former on some site lists when concentrated.

materials.name: S-Methylisothiourea
materials.note: May release methanethiol (toxic, flammable, strong odour) under basic or hot conditions.
materials.citation: Process safety literature (licensed source to be confirmed)

materials.name: Dimethyl sulfoxide
materials.note: Decomposition can be autocatalytic; acids, bases and some salts lower its onset.
materials.citation: Process safety literature (licensed source to be confirmed)

materials.name: Potassium permanganate
materials.note: Strong oxidiser. Oxidises chloride to chlorine.

materials.name: Manganese dioxide
materials.note: Fine solid waste. The filter cake can retain unreacted permanganate.
materials.citation: Process safety literature (licensed source to be confirmed)

materials.name: Sodium hydroxide
materials.note: Strong base. Dissolution in water is exothermic.

materials.name: Diisobutylaluminium hydride
materials.note: Pyrophoric (neat). Reacts violently with water and protic solvents, releasing isobutane and hydrogen.

materials.name: Aluminium hydroxide
materials.citation: Process safety literature (licensed source to be confirmed)

materials.name: Isobutane
materials.note: Flammable gas (bp about −12 °C). Dissolves when cold and is released on warming.

materials.name: Potassium sodium tartrate tetrahydrate
materials.note: Used to break aluminium emulsions in work-up.

rules.finding: Strong bases can lower the decomposition onset of DMSO; the decomposition may be autocatalytic.
rules.control: DSC and ARC of the actual mixture; keep Tp well below the measured onset; limit hold time at temperature.
rules.citation: Process safety literature on DMSO mixtures (licensed source to be confirmed)

rules.finding: Acids can lower the decomposition onset of DMSO.
rules.control: DSC of the mixture before scale-up.
rules.citation: Process safety literature on DMSO mixtures (licensed source to be confirmed)

rules.finding: DMSO is incompatible with strong oxidisers.
rules.control: Test for residual oxidant before any DMSO step.

rules.finding: A strong oxidiser with a flammable solvent: exothermic oxidation of the solvent, and accumulation if a solid oxidant is dosed cold.
rules.control: Dose the oxidant in portions under reaction calorimetry, with temperature-controlled addition.
Reaction calorimetry with the real dosing mode.
Remove acid and chloride before the oxidation (in-process control).

rules.finding: A strongly exothermic redox reaction, even when it is the intended quench.
rules.control: Controlled, temperature-limited quench with a defined end-point test.

rules.finding: A violent reaction releasing flammable gas.
rules.control: Controlled quench at low temperature under inert gas; vent sizing for the gas released.

rules.finding: An ignition source for flammable vapour.

rules.control: Slow acid addition; check headspace and vent capacity.

reactionClasses.name: Oxidation, sulfide to sulfone (permanganate) (typical range −350 to −550 kJ/mol)
Substitution by a sulfonamide anion (typical range −80 to −160 kJ/mol)
Ester reduction by aluminium hydride, with quench (typical range −250 to −400 kJ/mol)
